stemBlocks.value: The simple interest on $18 000 for 4 years is $5 040. a. Calculate the rate percent per annum.  b. Calculate the total amount at the end of 4 years.
Think first: You are given the interest and asked for the rate, so rearrange the simple interest formula instead of using it forwards.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p016-q01 from workbook page 16.

solutionSteps.instruction: Write down the simple interest formula.

strategyBlocks.value: Substitute the known values into I = PRT/100 and solve for R, then add the interest to the principal to get the amount.

whyThisWorks.value: Simple interest grows by the same fixed amount every year because it is always charged on the original principal, which is why I = PRT/100 is linear in each of P, R and T. That linearity is what lets the formula be rearranged for any single unknown. The amount is not a new calculation: it is the principal returned plus all the interest it earned.

commonErrors.misconception: Treating $5 040 as the amount rather than the interest and subtracting it from $18 000.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Treating $5 040 as the amount rather than the interest and subtracting it from $18 000.

commonErrors.misconception: Forgetting the ÷ 100 and getting a rate of 0.07%.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Forgetting the ÷ 100 and getting a rate of 0.07%.

commonErrors.misconception: Giving $5 040 as the final answer to part b.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Giving $5 040 as the final answer to part b.

examTip.value: Write I = PRT/100 out in full and label which letter is unknown before substituting — it turns every simple interest question into the same one-line rearrangement.
